title: Passage retrieval
content: Passage retrieval is the step in which a search or answer system selects specific sections of a page, in place of the whole page, to answer a query.

meta.why: Google describes passage ranking as a system that identifies individual sections of a page to judge relevance, which means a section deep in a long page can be the section that gets used.
meta.example: A long guide to warehouse software contains one section on barcode scanning, and that section is selected for a question about barcodes.
meta.check: Give each section a heading that names its subject and open the section with the fact a reader came for.
meta.limitation: Google documents passage ranking for Search, and that description does not cover how other answer engines select passages.
meta.sources: Google Search Central: guide to Google Search ranking systems | https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ranking-systems-guide | Platform documentation
